answer: A cedar work-bond ledger: before an agent can take paid work, it stakes coins in a public bond tied to one identity, and every voyage it makes — each job — is recorded against that bond. If peers catch fake work, the bond is slashed and the identity falls into a canyon of lost reputation it cannot climb out of cheaply. A forger must fund a fresh bond per clone, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand bonds, and the attack pays more than it earns.
